summary: Sandbridge Health — repeated 5xx + client retry amplification led to duplicate completions and invoice spike
description: Issue summary: Sandbridge Health (dedicated customer) experienced a 20-minute period of elevated 5xx responses from the inference endpoint which coincided with a 3x billing increase and multiple duplicate completions returned to their users. Impact: customer-visible duplicate replies (same prompt returned twice with different response IDs), elevated token billing for the window, and large user-facing latency spikes. Timeline (high level): 2026-03-05T18:02Z - first 502 spike observed in us-east serving cluster; 18:05Z - Sandbridge opened a support chat and reported duplicate completions; 18:08Z - Support triaged as P0 and routed to SRE/Runtime on-call; 18:12Z - automatic fallback routing triggered from primary quantized variant to compatibility variant; 18:18Z - circuit-breaker misclassification allowed duplicated retry path; 18:22Z - mitigation (disable aggressive fallback and throttle retries) applied; 18:30Z - visible error rates returned to baseline. Steps to reproduce (customer pattern): 1) Send high-concurrency streaming generation requests pinned to redwood-open-7b-quantized with idempotency header X-Req-Id; 2) During transient kernel-selection failure the gateway returned 502; 3) Client retried at the SDK layer without preserving idempotency header; 4) Routing fallback sent retry to a different model variant, producing a second (distinct) completion. Logs and artifacts: request traces, streaming logs, and billing deltas attached on Confluence page. Investigation notes: initial hypothesis focused on autoscale latency causing 502s; deeper traces show a transient kernel-selection OOM on a subset of quantized workers leading to 502/503. The API gateway retried the request to an available host which returned a different model variant. The customer's SDK retried client-side without keeping the original idempotency X-Req-Id header, which prevented dedup logic from de-duplicating retries. Root cause: three contributing factors - (1) kernel-selection edge-case produced transient 5xxs on quantized pool, (2) gateway fallback policy routed retries to a different compatible variant, (3) client-side retry behavior dropped idempotency metadata, allowing duplicate completions to be billed. Resolution: ramped down automatic fallback policy for the quantized pool; applied a short-lived rate-limit/quick-shed to thin out retry storms; coordinated with Sandbridge to apply an SDK patch ensuring idempotency header persistence. Billing remediation: flagged the affected window for manual review and issued a credit for the excess token usage after customer agreement. Follow-up: runbook updates and longer-term fixes scheduled.
